slides.title: Roles
slides.html: Each phone has one role, picked on Your role the first time Drones opens, and Drones then shows only that role's pages. The FOO, the forward observer officer, asks for drones. The HQ hands requests to the teams and sets corridors and quotas, and a TOC, a platoon's tactical operations centre, hands them to its own teams. In a Drone team the navigator plans, runs and reports the flights, and the Pilot flies by bearing and distance on the team's second phone.

slides.title: Requests
slides.html: A request asks for a Strike or a Recon on an enemy mark or a drawn area, with a Priority and, under To, whom to ask. The FOO sends it, and it waits for the HQ, a TOC or a drone team on their Requests page and in OpenDefence Main's Inbox. The asker follows each step under Sent in the Inbox. A request that no team takes lapses after two hours.

slides.title: Corridors
slides.html: A corridor is the area where a team may fly, for set hours. It shows as a shaded area on every phone that follows the drone feed, the Data Sync feed that carries missions, corridors and quotas between phones. The HQ draws corridors, and a TOC draws them for its own unit and the units under it. A plan uses the corridor that holds the target, or goes ahead with a note when none does, and the pilot sees how far the drone is from the corridor's edge.

slides.title: Quotas
slides.html: A quota gives a forward observer, or a whole unit, a set number of requests a day to one team. Only the HQ gives quotas, and the team needs a corridor first. On the Request sheet, that team then comes first under To, with a line saying how many requests are left today.

slides.title: Missions and plans
slides.html: A mission is one drone flight on a request, named like Strike 1 or Recon 4. The team's plan proposes the drone, the time window and the route, and checks the drone's Range and, with Weather lookups on, the Weather in the forecast of the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI). Problems such as No go weather are listed before sending, but the team decides. Missions then follows the mission from take-off to the team's report.

slides.title: Drone types
slides.html: A drone team lists the drones it has as types, each with its frame, payload, link and limits such as range and flight time, and a count. Plans use these types and their limits, and the HQ and the TOC see them with the team's status. Attack, Bomber and Multi-role drones are armed and can fly strikes. A drone used or lost comes off the count by itself.

slides.title: What everyone sees
slides.html: Every phone on the drone feeds shows the corridors, each mission's route and the sortie circle around its target. The drone shows from its own track, the position it sends, or as a marker its team moves by hand, and the route's name says Executing while it flies. What the team marks and sends arrives as an enemy mark, and Watch on a flying mission opens its video. Phones without OpenDefence UAVOps see the map items too.

slides.title: A plugin on OpenDefence Main
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps is a separate plugin that works through OpenDefence Main. Its units come from the ORBAT, the order of battle an admin sets up in OpenDefence Main, and requests are made on OpenDefence Main's Request sheet. Its rows in the Inbox show what waits for you, here under For you, and under Sent how your own requests went. An admin can switch Quotas and corridors off in OpenDefence Main for a unit that runs no TOCs, which turns off quotas, corridors and the TOC role.
